fix: and no one defended this act of Alexander’s as just.
reason: Seam word Ἀλεξάνδρου completes οὐδεὶς clause of ch. 2; genitive belongs here.

fix: They therefore, after a short time and with some help received, once again lived in their homeland in safety.
reason: ‘After Alexander’s campaign’ invented from seam word; drop it, keep original wording otherwise.

fix: For all who fall into unexpected disasters, both collectively and individually, should be counted as unlucky;
reason: μέν/δέ contrasts ἀκληρεῖν (unlucky) with ἀτυχεῖν (unfortunate); English made both ‘unfortunate’, a contradiction.

fix: Peloponnesians, Boeotians, Phocians, [...], Locrians,
reason: Greek has lost ethnic in -εῖς between Phocians and Locrians; mark lacuna.

fix: [...] not only in the number [...] of earlier ones, but also in [...]; in a word, they were not unlucky but suffered a misfortune as shameful and disgraceful as could be.
reason: Lacunae smoothed, ‘in every way’ invented; οὐκ ἠκλήρησαν ἀλλ᾽ ἠτύχησαν must keep the defined distinction.

fix: Thus, stripped of all good things, some [...], while others even [...] at that time admitted the rods and axes into their cities, willingly [...]
reason: ‘Hunger’, ‘desperation’ invented over gaps; παρεδέξαντο = admitted. ἐθελο[...] likely ‘willingly’ but broken: translator decides.

fix: because of the excess of their own mistakes—if one should call them their own.
reason: εἰ χρὴ λέγειν ἰδίων qualifies ‘own’, explained by the next sentence.

fix: when I, of all people, ought to have concealed the mistakes of the Greeks.
reason: οἷς agrees with ἡμῖν: the writer himself is the one who ought to conceal.

fix: For the more widely the transmission of what is written reaches people, and the longer it lasts, compared with what is said for the moment,
reason: Genitive of comparison τῶν πρὸς καιρὸν λεγομένων dropped; restore with minimal change.

fix: And, they say, those who love learning seek continuity and look forward to hearing the end of the account;
reason: Infinitives continue the critics’ reported claim, which Polybius then rejects; ‘But’ made it his view.

fix: rests for men who labor hard.
reason: No lacuna: ἀνδρῶν (first word of ch. 6) completes the phrase.

fix: That is why the greatest historians of old seem to me
reason: Opening phrase invented from seam word ἀνδρῶν; restore inferential διό, otherwise keep wording.

fix: and to give every assurance that we will do what is ordered
reason: πᾶν ἀναδέχεσθαι διότι: διότι is ‘that’ after the verb of guaranteeing, not causal.

fix: Hasdrubal said that Gulussa did not understand the situation.
reason: αὐτόν (accusative subject) is Gulussa; English made Hasdrubal the ignorant one.

fix: or the forces in the field;
reason: Narrator’s aside, not Hasdrubal’s speech; ὅτι σώζονται is bracketed for deletion; ὑπαίθρων = in the field.

fix: For the gods, he said, would not stand by and see them so openly wronged in breach of the treaty, but would give them many opportunities for salvation.
reason: σφᾶς = the Carthaginians, wronged by treaty-breach; English made the gods treaty-breakers.

fix: that one would not easily find leaders of affairs more alike than those of the Greeks and of the Carthaginians at that time
reason: Genitive of comparison, plural leaders; not ‘two men’ found ‘among’ them.

fix: When Aurelius and his fellow envoys arrived from the Peloponnese
reason: τῶν περὶ τὸν Αὐρήλιον πρεσβευτῶν are Aurelius’ own embassy returning, not envoys sent to him.

fix: assumed that the Romans [...] by way of pretense, because the war in Carthage was still unfinished
reason: Lacuna *** where the infinitive stood; English supplied ‘were acting’.

fix: the justice of what Sextus and his colleagues were saying
reason: οἱ περὶ τὸν Σέξτον are the envoys themselves.

fix: men who were the worst of every city, as if picked out on purpose
reason: ὥσπερ ἐπίτηδες is comparison (‘as if on purpose’), not a statement of fact.

fix: and there confer with the Lacedaemonians [...] so that some agreed settlement
reason: Lacuna *** after Λακεδαιμονίοις smoothed over.

fix: For they ought not to fear the Lacedaemonians or the Romans so much as those among their own people who cooperated with the enemy;
reason: Accusatives are objects of ἀγωνιᾶν with οὐ οὕτως ὡς; English inverted who fears.

fix: Philetaerus
reason: Φιλεταίρου = Philetaerus; misspelled.
